name: The Stow household
head: stow_william_h

arrival.note: 'About 1833' is the hotel chronology's phrase and the word 'about' is carried here as a year-precision value rather than smoothed into a date.

reason_for_coming.value: To build and keep a hotel in the boom
reason_for_coming.note: He built the house he then kept, in the two years when the town's population went from about 350 to 3,265. The inference is the motive.

lives_at.note: A landlord lived in his house; not stated.

present_on_scene_date.note: Operating the house across the scene date.

persons.name: William H. Stow

occupation.note: The hotel chronology says outright that the Western Hotel was 'built and operated by W.H. Stow'. He is therefore both the builder and the landlord, and this record carries the keeping rather than the building because the keeping is what he was doing on the scene date.

persons.note: Both sources have him building and operating the house, and he came to Chicago about 1833, so he is present at the scene date on either build date this project holds for the Western. Andreas's later city rosters carry a William H. Stow as an alderman in 1839, which corroborates the man's continuing residence and says nothing about 1835. OLD SETTLERS, 1882 — A DATE OF DEATH, AND NOTHING ABOUT 1835. John Wentworth's roll of old settlers who had died since 1 January 1881, kept for the Calumet Club and printed in the Chicago Tribune of 25 April 1882, carries “William H. stow, Aug. 18, 1881.”. That corroborates a Chicago residence before 1840 and fixes the END of this life, which this record did not carry; it is not an arrival and it places nobody in the town on 1 July 1835. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json).

research_note: A BUILDER-LANDLORD, WHICH IS A COMMON EARLY-CHICAGO PATTERN AND ONE THE OCCUPATION FIELD CANNOT SHOW. Stow put the Western Hotel up and then ran it, and this dataset also holds western_hotel_stable under his name. The occupation vocabulary makes a single choice, so the building half of his life is in this note. NOTHING HERE ABOUT HIS FAMILY: a hotel of forty feet frontage with a wagon yard behind it was not run by one man alone, and every other person in it - servants, hostlers, cooks, his own household - is unattested and belongs to the inferred phase.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. The value is the volume's own line, split by its crosswalk on the entry's punctuation. These volumes set the trade first and its qualifiers after it on the same line, so the split may carry an employer, a market or a corner along with the trade. The printed entry is quoted beside the value for exactly that reason: the split is checkable against it, and neither is read into an 1835 claim.
